findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/managed-review-evidence.ts:236-244 — the F-127 terminal-retention-GC mitigation does not restore post-GC verifiability, and its own comment understates why. Empirically confirmed: after pruneExpiredManagedHostRuns deletes the run directory, re-verifying already-imported managed evidence returns valid=false with reason 'story_mismatch,bad_shape,digest_mismatch,stale_material,artifact_subject_mismatch,producer_owned_required'. The comment admits one blocker (proposal is still read from the deleted directory, so semanticDigestValid/subjectMatches refuse), but omits a second independent one: externalImportSealMatches (line 343-346) reads evidence-binding.json and evidence-binding.seal.json from the same deleted directory and returns false when absent, and the REVIEW gate at core/review-run.ts:1527 ALWAYS passes `evidence`, so that predicate is always evaluated. Consequence is an unrecoverable in-flow deadlock, not a degraded read: managed_receipt_invalid is absent from SUPERSEDED_PASS_ISSUE_CODES, so it short-circuits at review-run.ts:1698 (`return true`) and remains in evidenceState.invalid permanently — fresh evidence, resolved/dismissed findings and new review rounds cannot supersede it — and core/machine.ts:790 blocks REVIEW→TEST whenever invalid.length > 0, before any blocking-severity filter or round decay. This is the same mechanism the code documents for F-100. No recovery path is documented in docs/host-run-usage.md or the design doc, and no test exercises verifyManagedReviewEvidence after a reclaim (grep for F-127/reclaimed in managed-review-evidence-smoke.ts returns nothing). Severity medium, not high, because reachability is narrow: it needs an explicit `doctor --repair` AND a terminal run older than the 90-day MANAGED_HOST_RUN_TERMINAL_RETENTION_MS whose evidence is still gate-consumed. Not a doc-promise violation — managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md 'Retention and trust boundary' promises only 'the minimal receipt plus evidence-binding digest' and never post-GC re-verifiability. The defect is that the mitigation's stated goal is unmet, the residual risk is under-described in the comment, and the reclaimed path is untested.
